constraints.meaning: At least one number, at most 10,000.
constraints.impact: Square-then-sort, O(n log n), is fast enough. Interviewers still expect the O(n) two-pointer pass, which uses the sorted input.

constraints.meaning: Values can be negative, zero or positive.
constraints.impact: A square is at most 10⁸, so it fits in int. Negative values are the reason the squares are not already sorted: (−4)² = 16 is bigger than 3² = 9.

constraints.text: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
constraints.meaning: Each value is greater than or equal to the one before it. Equal values can sit next to each other.
constraints.impact: This is the key clue. The largest square is always at one of the two ends: the most negative value or the most positive value. So two pointers at the ends can find the squares from largest to smallest.

bruteForce.summary: square every value, then sort the squares: O(n log n) with a library sort. It throws away the fact that nums is already sorted. The code below sorts with insertion sort so each comparison can be counted.
